claim: Most genetic studies in model organisms have focused on cell-intrinsic gene functions and mechanisms.
source: Most have focused on cell-intrinsic gene functions and mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated as background context in the abstract without specific supporting data in the manuscript.

claim: Much less is known about how transformed or functionally disrupted cells interact with healthy ones toward a favorable or pathological outcome.
source: Much less is known about how transformed, or otherwise functionally disrupted, cells interact with healthy ones toward a favorable or pathological outcome.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: Limited knowledge about cell-cell interactions in disease contexts is largely due to technical limitations.
source: This is largely due to technical limitations.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the knowledge gap.

claim: The new genetic tools developed permit efficient multiplexed gain- and loss-of-function genetic perturbations with separable spatial and temporal control.
source: We developed new genetic tools in Drosophila melanogaster that permit efficient multiplexed gain- and loss-of-function genetic perturbations with separable spatial and temporal control.
evidence: This is the main claim of the study, supported by experimental demonstrations throughout the manuscript.

claim: The novel tool-set is independent of the commonly used GAL4/UAS system.
source: Importantly, our novel tool-set is independent of the commonly used GAL4/UAS system, freeing the latter for additional, non-autonomous, genetic manipulations
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 3 and throughout the Results section.

claim: The tool is built into a single strain, allowing one-generation interrogation of non-autonomous effects.
source: and is built into a single strain, allowing one-generation interrogation of non-autonomous effects.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the experimental design shown in Figures 1 and 5.

claim: The design opens up efficient genome-wide screens on any deleterious phenotype once plasmid or genome engineering is used to place desired miRNA(s) or ORF(s) into the genotype.
source: Altogether, our design opens up efficient genome-wide screens on any deleterious phenotype, once plasmid or genome engineering is used to place the desired miRNA(s) or ORF(s) into our genotype.
evidence: This is a prospective claim based on the demonstrated functionality of the system.

claim: The tools were specifically developed to study extrinsic effects on neural tumor growth.
source: Specifically, we developed tools to study extrinsic effects on neural tumor growth but the strategy presented has endless applications within and beyond neurobiology, and in other model organisms.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the neural tumor experiments in Figures 2, 5, and 6.

claim: No available genetic tool up to now was suited for efficient large-scale screening for cell non-autonomous effects on a developmentally deleterious genotype.
source: Despite numerous and versatile genetic mosaic strategies available for genetically amenable model organism Drosophila melanogaster, none up to now was suited for efficient large-scale screening for cell non-autonomous effects on a developmentally deleterious genotype.
evidence: This is stated as the motivation for the study based on existing knowledge of available tools.

claim: Non-autonomous effects are more challenging to investigate than cell-autonomous effects due to the requirement for combinations of genetic manipulations.
source: Given the requirement for combinations of genetic manipulations, non-autonomous effects are more challenging to investigate yet well known to play crucial roles in development and disease contexts such as cancer.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge explaining the technical challenge.

claim: Non-autonomous effects play crucial roles in development and disease contexts such as cancer.
source: Given the requirement for combinations of genetic manipulations, non-autonomous effects are more challenging to investigate yet well known to play crucial roles in development and disease contexts such as cancer.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The challenge of studying non-autonomous effects applies to any tissue but is particularly evident in the central nervous system (CNS).
source: The challenge applies to any tissue but is particularly evident in the central nervous system (CNS) due to diversity of cell types and uniqueness of each lineage with respect to gene expression, size, projection patterns, as well as lethality frequently associated with their disruption.
evidence: This is stated as reasoning for why the CNS is particularly challenging.

claim: The CNS is particularly challenging for studying non-autonomous effects due to diversity of cell types and uniqueness of each lineage with respect to gene expression, size, projection patterns, and lethality frequently associated with their disruption.
source: The challenge applies to any tissue but is particularly evident in the central nervous system (CNS) due to diversity of cell types and uniqueness of each lineage with respect to gene expression, size, projection patterns, as well as lethality frequently associated with their disruption.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about CNS complexity.

claim: No available genetic tool allowed large-scale screening for non-autonomous effects on neural tumor growth because animals harbouring neural tumors cannot be kept as a stable stock.
source: To illustrate in our specific case: no available genetic tool allowed large-scale screening for non-autonomous effects on neural tumor growth as animals harbouring neural tumors cannot be kept as a stable stock.
evidence: This is stated as the specific problem addressed by the study.

claim: Drosophila has been a canvas for pioneering mosaic tools based on heterologous binary systems for transcriptional activation or recombination.
source: Drosophila has been a canvas for pioneering mosaic tools, at the heart of which lie heterologous binary systems for transcriptional activation or recombination (Griffin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with citation support.

claim: Transcriptional activation systems include the yeast transcription factor GAL4 and its binding site UAS, the bacterial LexA/LexA Operator, and the fungal QF/QUAS system.
source: Transcriptional activation systems include the yeast transcription factor GAL4 and its binding site, named Upstream Activating Sequence (UAS); the bacterial LexA/LexA Operator (LexAop); and the fungal QF/QUAS system (Brand and Perrimon, 1993; Yagi et al., 2010; Potter et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Recombination systems include the bacteriophage Cre recombinase and its loxP target, the yeast Flippase/Flippase Recognition Target sites (FLP/FRT) and its variant mFLP5/mFRT71, and other yeast recombinases (KD, R, B2, and B3) and their cognate recognition sites.
source: Recombination systems include the bacteriophage Cre recombinase and its loxP target; the yeast Flippase/Flippase Recognition Target sites (FLP/FRT) and its variant mFLP5/mFRT71; and other yeast recombinases (KD, R, B2, and B3) and their cognate recognition sites (Golic and Lindquist, 1989; Siegal and Hartl, 1996; Hadjieconomou et al., 2011; Nern et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The modularity of binary systems grants them combinatorial flexibility.
source: The modularity of binary systems grants them combinatorial flexibility, and ingenious Boolean logic gates between recombination and transcriptional activation/silencing systems have expanded their applications (eg., Struhl and Basler, 1993; Lee and Luo, 1999; Griffin et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2009; Yagi et al., 2010; Hadjieconomou et al., 2011; Hampel et al., 2011); von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Awasaki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Boolean logic gates between recombination and transcriptional activation/silencing systems have expanded the applications of binary systems.
source: The modularity of binary systems grants them combinatorial flexibility, and ingenious Boolean logic gates between recombination and transcriptional activation/silencing systems have expanded their applications (eg., Struhl and Basler, 1993; Lee and Luo, 1999; Griffin et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2009; Yagi et al., 2010; Hadjieconomou et al., 2011; Hampel et al., 2011); von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Awasaki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Binary systems have been extensively employed to perform large-scale screens using publically available UAS libraries to provide molecular understanding into numerous conserved cell intrinsic processes.
source: Binary systems have been extensively employed to perform large-scale screens using publically available UAS libraries to provide molecular understanding into numerous conserved cell intrinsic processes (St Johnston, 2002; Kawakami et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Genome-wide screens remain to be applied to extrinsic processes modifying an adverse genotype.
source: Genome-wide screens remain to be applied to extrinsic processes modifying an adverse genotype.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Tumor reproducibility requires control over lineage, induction time and consistency of levels of downregulation of tumor-suppressors and/or upregulation of oncogenes.
source: Tumor reproducibility requires control over lineage, induction time and consistency of levels of downregulation of tumor-suppressors and/or upregulation of oncogenes.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for the experimental design.

claim: The FOFO design achieves desired features via the employment of two very efficient transcriptional termination sequences (STOP cassettes) upstream of an oncogenic sequence and reporter.
source: Our design presented achieves the desired features via the employment of two very efficient transcriptional termination sequences (STOP cassettes) upstream of an oncogenic sequence and reporter.
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in Figures 2 and throughout the Results section.

claim: Each STOP cassette is flanked by recombinase target sequences selective for two distinct recombinases, one constitutively expressed in selected lineages (conferring spatial specificity) and the other whose expression is induced by heat-shock (conferring rapid temporal resolution).
source: Each STOP cassette is flanked by recombinase target sequences selective for two distinct recombinases, one constitutively expressed in selected lineages, conferring spatial specificity; the other whose expression is induced by heat-shock (hs), conferring rapid temporal resolution.
evidence: This is the design principle demonstrated in Figure 1 and validated experimentally.

claim: The new genetic tools were tested and refined by recapitulating two well-established Drosophila neural tumor models.
source: We tested and refined the new genetic tools by recapitulating two well-established Drosophila neural tumor models, one generated by downregulation of the homeodomain transcription factor Prospero (Pros), which can lead to tumorigenesis in all neural lineages (of which there are around 100 per central brain lobe); another by downregulation of the NHL-domain protein Brain tumor (Brat), whose depletion leads to tumorigenesis specifically in so-called type II lineages (of which there are eight per brain lobe (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Sousa-Nunes et al., 2010).
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in Figures 2, 5, and 6.

claim: Downregulation of Prospero can lead to tumorigenesis in all neural lineages.
source: one generated by downregulation of the homeodomain transcription factor Prospero (Pros), which can lead to tumorigenesis in all neural lineages (of which there are around 100 per central brain lobe)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and demonstrated in the experiments.

claim: There are around 100 neural lineages per central brain lobe.
source: one generated by downregulation of the homeodomain transcription factor Prospero (Pros), which can lead to tumorigenesis in all neural lineages (of which there are around 100 per central brain lobe)
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Downregulation of Brain tumor (Brat) leads to tumorigenesis specifically in type II lineages.
source: another by downregulation of the NHL-domain protein Brain tumor (Brat), whose depletion leads to tumorigenesis specifically in so-called type II lineages (of which there are eight per brain lobe (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Sousa-Nunes et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation and demonstrated in experiments.

claim: There are eight type II lineages per brain lobe.
source: another by downregulation of the NHL-domain protein Brain tumor (Brat), whose depletion leads to tumorigenesis specifically in so-called type II lineages (of which there are eight per brain lobe (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (Sousa-Nunes et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The design can be multiplexed beyond two to produce further spatial intersections or multiple temporal steps.
source: Starting from the units presented here our design can be multiplexed beyond two to produce further spatial intersections, or multiple temporal steps, along with any assemblies of gene expression downstream (downregulation and/or upregulation, plus reporter labeling).
evidence: This is a prospective claim based on the demonstrated modularity of the system.

claim: The strategy is applicable to other tissues, organisms and biological questions.
source: This strategy is therefore of broad interest, applicable to other tissues, organisms and biological questions, opening-up large-scale screening for non-autonomous effects.
evidence: This is a prospective claim based on the general principles of the design.

claim: Expression of deleterious sequences by the ubiquitous strong actin5C promoter was blocked by two stringent STOP cassettes.
source: Key to the design of this tumor-generating tool is that expression of deleterious sequences by the ubiquitous strong actin5C promoter, was blocked by not one (as commonly done), but two stringent STOP cassettes.
evidence: This is the design principle shown in Figure 1a and validated experimentally.

claim: Each STOP cassette was flanked by the selective recombination sites FRT and mFRT71, specifically recognized by FLP and mFLP5, respectively.
source: Each STOP cassette was flanked by the selective recombination sites FRT and mFRT71, specifically recognized by FLP and mFLP5, respectively (Hadjieconomou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is the design principle shown in Figure 1a with citation support.

claim: The design is called 'FOFO', for Flp-Out-mFlp5-Out.
source: We called this design 'FOFO', for Flp-Out-mFlp5-Out.
evidence: This is the naming convention introduced by the authors.

claim: Expression would be unblocked only in the presence of the two Flippases, with spatiotemporal control achieved by lineage-restricted expression of FLP and hs-induction of mFLP5.
source: The prediction was that expression would be unblocked only in the presence of the two Flippases, with spatiotemporal control achieved by lineage-restricted expression of FLP and hs-induction of mFLP5 (Figure 1a).
evidence: This prediction is validated experimentally in Figures 2 and 5.

claim: Multicistronic expression of oncogenic and reporter proteins can be easily achieved by sandwiching T2A peptide codons between coding sequences.
source: Multicistronic expression of oncogenic and reporter proteins can be easily achieved by sandwiching T2A peptide (González et al., 2011; Diao and White, 2012) codons between coding sequences (cds).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Artificial miRs consist of 21 bp sequences designed for RNA interference, embedded into a sequence backbone of a naturally occurring miR.
source: Artificial miRs consist of 21 bp sequences designed for RNA interference, embedded into a sequence backbone of a naturally occurring miR
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about miRNA design.

claim: Artificial miRs are very effective in downregulating gene expression, more so than long double-stranded RNAs.
source: they are very effective in downregulating gene expression (more so than long double-stranded RNAs; Ni et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Artificial miRs can be transcribed by RNA polymerase II.
source: can be transcribed by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) (Lee et al., 2004)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Artificial miRs can be concatenated for synergistic effect.
source: and can be concatenated for synergistic effect (Chen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Placing the EGFP cds downstream of an intron increases transcript expression.
source: We placed the EGFP cds downstream of an intron as this increases transcript expression (Haley et al., 2010)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Placing miRs in an intron has the advantage of being able to host miRs without disrupting transcript stability by their processing, unlike when miRs are placed in the 3' untranslated region.
source: and has the additional advantage of being able to host miRs without disrupting transcript stability by their processing, unlike when miRs are placed in the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) (Bejarano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: miRs targeting GAL4 were included so that if the GAL4 expression domain overlapped with the tumor domain, GAL4 would be silenced within the tumor.
source: Wishing to study strictly cell non-autonomous effects employing the GAL4/UAS system, we included miRs targeting GAL4 as well as those targeting a tumor suppressor (two miRs per target). Therefore, if the GAL4 expression domain overlapped with the tumor domain, GAL4 would be silenced within the tumor.
evidence: This design principle is validated experimentally in Figure 3.

claim: Two miRs per target were used for tumor suppressors and GAL4.
source: we included miRs targeting GAL4 as well as those targeting a tumor suppressor (two miRs per target).
evidence: This is stated as part of the design and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: miRs targeting the neural tumor suppressors pros or brat were used for tumor induction and those targeting CD2 were used as control.
source: miRs targeting the neural tumor suppressors pros or brat were used for tumor induction and those targeting CD2 were used as control (Yu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as the experimental design with citation support.

claim: All constructs generated for this study were flanked by gypsy insulators to minimize position effects and enhance expression.
source: To minimize position effects and enhance expression, all constructs generated for this study were flanked by gypsy insulators and integrated into the Drosophila genome by PhiC3-mediated transgenesis, selecting sites reported to produce low basal and high induced expression (Markstein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as part of the design methodology with citation support.

claim: All constructs were integrated into the Drosophila genome by PhiC3-mediated transgenesis, selecting sites reported to produce low basal and high induced expression.
source: To minimize position effects and enhance expression, all constructs generated for this study were flanked by gypsy insulators and integrated into the Drosophila genome by PhiC3-mediated transgenesis, selecting sites reported to produce low basal and high induced expression (Markstein et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as part of the methodology with citation support.

claim: Central to the success of the FOFO strategy is the efficacy of the STOP cassettes.
source: Central to the success of this strategy is the efficacy of the STOP cassettes.
evidence: This is stated as a key requirement and validated experimentally in Figure 2.

claim: Some degree of STOP leakiness can be afforded to simply label cells or to generate a deleterious genetic perturbation by means of a cross, but it is absolutely incompatible with harbouring a 'locked' deleterious perturbation within a stable stock.
source: For each, we used tandem transcriptional terminators, as others before us. Whereas some degree of STOP leakiness can be afforded to simply label cells or to generate a deleterious genetic perturbation by means of a cross, it is absolutely incompatible with our aim of harbouring a 'locked' deleterious perturbation within a stable stock.
evidence: This is stated as a design constraint.

claim: Removal of the lamin cds from the STOP cassette used in Flybow resulted in failure to terminate transcription despite concatenated hsp70Aa and hsp27 terminators, seen by EGFP expression in the absence of Flippase.
source: Removal of the lamin cds from the STOP cassette used in Flybow (Hadjieconomou et al., 2011) resulted in failure to terminate transcription despite concatenated hsp70Aa and hsp27 terminators, seen by EGFP expression in the absence of Flippase (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with citation.

claim: Concatenation of hsp70Bb and SV40 terminators successfully precluded unintended EGFP expression.
source: In contrast, concatenation of hsp70Bb and SV40 terminators, successfully precluded unintended EGFP expression.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: In the presence of both hs-FLP and hs-mFLP5 and only after hs, extensive patches of EGFP were observed in all FOFO1.0 transgenics.
source: FOFO1.0 was tested with publicly available stocks of FLP and mFLP5 both under the control of the strong hs promoter. Encouragingly, in the presence of both hs-FLP and hs-mFLP5 and only after hs, extensive patches of EGFP were observed in all transgenics (FOFO1.0-CD2miRs-GAL4miRs, FOFO1.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs and FOFO1.0-bratmiRs-GAL4miRs) (Figure 2b)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2b.

claim: Occasional single cells labeled with EGFP could be seen in the absence of hs (average of 0.3 per brain lobe).
source: occasional single cells labeled with EGFP could be seen in the absence of hs (average of 0.3 per brain lobe; n = 240 pooling data for FOFO1.0 and FOFO2.0 carrying CD2miRs, prosmiRs or bratmiRs with no significant difference between genotypes).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation from the experiments.

claim: Only in the presence of the oncogenic miRs were ectopic neural stem cells (NSCs) observed.
source: Furthermore, only in the presence of the oncogenic miRs were ectopic neural stem cells (NSCs) observed (Figure 2b white-boxed insets: note NSC density within EGFP patches in brains expressing oncogenic miRs versus controls).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2b.

claim: Ectopic NSCs were sometimes observed outside the EGFP domain in FOFO1.0 carrying prosmiRs or bratmiRs.
source: However, ectopic NSCs were sometimes observed also outside the EGFP domain in FOFO1.0 carrying prosmiRs or bratmiRs (Figure 2b yellow-boxed inset).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2b.

claim: Ectopic NSCs outside the EGFP domain were never seen in the absence of hs, indicating it was a Flippase-dependent process.
source: Because this was never seen in the absence of hs it was a Flippase-dependent process, likely due to inefficient termination of Pol II following excision of only one of the STOP cassettes.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The FOFO design, containing phenotype-inducing miRs ~ 200 bp downstream of STOP cassettes, is a sensitive reporter of Pol II readthrough.
source: We concluded that our design, containing phenotype-inducing miRs ~ 200 bp downstream of STOP cassettes, was a sensitive reporter of Pol II readthrough (Proudfoot, 2016) and that this STOP cassette was unsuitable for our purpose.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations with citation.

claim: The FOFO1.0 STOP cassette was unsuitable for the intended purpose.
source: We concluded that our design, containing phenotype-inducing miRs ~ 200 bp downstream of STOP cassettes, was a sensitive reporter of Pol II readthrough (Proudfoot, 2016) and that this STOP cassette was unsuitable for our purpose.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: FOFO2.0 contains two longer and potentially stronger STOP cassettes: the Flybow one including lamin cds and a concatenation of four SV40 terminators.
source: We next generated a FOFO2.0 version containing two longer and potentially stronger, STOP cassettes: the Flybow one including lamin cds and a concatenation of four SV40 terminators (Jackson et al., 2001; Hadjieconomou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as the design of FOFO2.0 with citation support and shown in Figure 2a.

claim: With FOFO2.0, in the presence of both hs-FLP and hs-mFLP5 and only after hs, extensive patches of EGFP were observed in all transgenics.
source: As with FOFO1.0, in the presence of both hs-FLP and hs-mFLP5 and only after hs, extensive patches of EGFP were observed in all FOFO2.0 transgenics
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2c.

claim: EGFP single-cell labeling frequency with FOFO2.0 was analogous to that for FOFO1.0.
source: EGFP single-cell labeling frequency was analogous to that for FOFO1.0
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between the two versions.

claim: With FOFO2.0, only in the presence of oncogenic miRs were ectopic NSCs observed.
source: and only in the presence of oncogenic miRs were ectopic NSCs observed (Figure 2c white-boxed insets).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2c.

claim: When a double hs of 1.5 hr each 24 hr apart was performed on FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs, tumors were occasionally seen in the presence of only hs-mFLP5 (one central brain lineage in 8 out of 12 brains, which amounts to a frequency of ~0.3%).
source: When we performed a double hs of 1.5 hr each 24 hr apart on FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs we occasionally saw tumors in the presence of only hs-mFLP5 (one central brain lineage in 8 out of 12 brains, which amounts to a frequency of ~0.3% as previously reported for cross-reactivity of hs-mFLP5 with FRT sites; Hadjieconomou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with citation.

claim: The ~0.3% frequency of tumors with only hs-mFLP5 was previously reported for cross-reactivity of hs-mFLP5 with FRT sites.
source: When we performed a double hs of 1.5 hr each 24 hr apart on FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs we occasionally saw tumors in the presence of only hs-mFLP5 (one central brain lineage in 8 out of 12 brains, which amounts to a frequency of ~0.3% as previously reported for cross-reactivity of hs-mFLP5 with FRT sites; Hadjieconomou et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: There was no leaky miR transcription in the absence of detectable EGFP, as evidenced by no differences in NSC numbers between WT and prosmiRs and bratmiRs central brains in the absence of hs or the presence of a single Flippase.
source: To ascertain that there was no leaky miR transcription in the absence of detectable EGFP, we counted the number of NSCs per larval central brain lobe and saw no differences between wild-type (WT) and prosmiRs and bratmiRs central brains, in the absence of hs or the presence of a single Flippase (or, in the few cases where hs-mFLP5 cross-reacted with FRT sites, outside the EGFP domain) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: With FOFO2.0, supernumerary NSCs were never observed outside the EGFP domain.
source: Crucially, with FOFO2.0 supernumerary NSCs were never observed outside the EGFP domain (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2c.

claim: The FOFO2.0 design confirmed low-frequency cross-reactivity between mFLP5 and FRT sites but largely blocked miR transcription in the absence of either Flippase and successfully unblocked it in the presence of both, with perfect correspondence to EGFP reporter expression.
source: In summary, the FOFO2.0 design confirmed low-frequency cross-reactivity between mFLP5 and FRT sites but largely blocked miR transcription in the absence of either Flippase and successfully unblocked it in the presence of both, with perfect correspondence to EGFP reporter expression.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Following heat-shock, RFP-negative patches were observed in perfect overlap with EGFP-labeled clones, as expected from efficient GAL4 knock-down.
source: Indeed, following heat-shock, RFP-negative patches were observed in perfect overlap with EGFP-labeled clones, as expected from efficient GAL4 knock-down (Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3.

claim: Few lineage-specific FLP lines are currently available.
source: Few lineage-specific FLP lines are currently available so we set out to generate some suited for our purpose.
evidence: This is stated as motivation for generating new lines.

claim: For type II lineages, the R19H09 and stg14 enhancers were previously described to be expressed therein.
source: For type II lineages, we used the R19H09 and stg14 enhancers previously described to be expressed therein (Bayraktar et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Induction of pros or brat tumors requires that these neural tumor suppressors be downregulated in progenitors, not in differentiated progeny.
source: Induction of pros or brat tumors requires that these neural tumor suppressors be downregulated in progenitors, not in differentiated progeny.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for the experimental design.

claim: Downregulation of pros should induce supernumerary NSCs in all central brain lineages (type I or II), whereas downregulation of brat should induce supernumerary NSCs only in type II.
source: Downregulation of pros should induce supernumerary NSCs in all central brain lineages (type I or II), whereas downregulation of brat should induce supernumerary NSCs only in type II.
evidence: This is stated as expected behavior based on known biology.

claim: A mutated form of FLP called FLP(D), which at position five contains an aspartic acid instead of glycine residue, is reported to be at least ten-fold more efficient than the original.
source: We employed a mutated form of FLP called FLP(D), which at position five contains an aspartic acid instead of glycine residue (Babineau et al., 1985) and is reported to be at least ten-fold more efficient than the original (Nern et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: In all cases, expression controlled by the hsp70 promoter was less widespread relative to that controlled by the DSCP.
source: In all cases, expression controlled by the hsp70 promoter was less widespread relative to that controlled by the DSCP (Figure 4), which could be due either to less background or sensitivity.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: Most newly generated enhancer-FLP lines containing the hsp70 promoter behaved as expected (no EGFP clusters containing supernumerary NSCs in the absence of hs).
source: Most lines behaved as expected (no EGFP clusters containing supernumerary NSCs in the absence of hs: 0/33 for R14E01; 0/41 for R73G11; 0/31 for R19H09; 0/30 for R51F05; 0/36 for R71A05)
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation from the experiments.

claim: Some enhancer-FLPs did very occasionally lead to induction of EGFP clusters containing supernumerary NSCs in the absence of hs (1/34 for R66B05; 5/39 for R12H06; 3/40 for R16C01; 4/28 for stg14), in all cases with a single spurious clone per brain.
source: but some enhancer-FLPs did very occasionally lead to induction of EGFP clusters containing supernumerary NSCs in the absence of hs (1/34 for R66B05; 5/39 for R12H06; 3/40 for R16C01; 4/28 for stg14); in all cases with a single spurious clone per brain.
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation from the experiments.

claim: FLP can cross-react with very low frequency with non-cognate mFRT71 sites (overall frequency of ~0.04% based on the number of such clones within the ~100 neural lineages per central brain).
source: This indicates that FLP can cross-react with very low frequency with non-cognate mFRT71 sites (overall frequency of ~0.04% based on the number of such clones within the ~100 neural lineages per central brain; INPs were not included in this calculation, accounting for which would result in an even lower frequency).
evidence: This is stated as a calculation based on experimental observations.

claim: FLP cross-reactivity with mFRT71 was never detected when crossing hs-FLP alone to FOFO2.0 lines even following long double heat-shocks.
source: This cross-reactivity was never detected when crossing hs-FLP alone to FOFO2.0 lines even following long double heat-shocks (Figure 2− figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: FLP cross-reactivity with mFRT71 is either due to the FLP(D) structural variation, its enhanced recombination efficiency, and/or the fact that it is provided constitutively by the spatially restricted enhancers as opposed to transiently via a hs-mediated pulse.
source: suggesting that this phenomenon is either due to the FLP(D) structural variation, its enhanced recombination efficiency, and/or the fact that it is provided constitutively by the spatially restricted enhancers as opposed to transiently via a hs-mediated pulse.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative explanation for the observed phenomenon.

claim: EGFP-labeled supernumerary NSCs were consistently observed following hs when FOFO2.0 transgenics recombined with hs-mFLP5 were crossed to enhancer-FLP(D) lines.
source: As expected, EGFP-labeled supernumerary NSCs were consistently observed following hs (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5a.

claim: It was possible to combine all transgenes in a single animal stock with the exception of R12H06-FLP(D) and FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs.
source: It was possible to combine all transgenes in a single animal stock with the exception of R12H06-FLP(D) and FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs, which was likely because this was the only one with a reasonable degree of tumor induction in the absence of heat-shock (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation with explanation, demonstrated in Figure 5b.

claim: Following heat-shock, patches of EGFP-labeled supernumerary NSCs were observed for all enhancer-FLP(D) lines with both hs-mFLP5;FOFO2.0-CD2miRs-GAL4miRs (controls) and hs-mFLP5;FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs but only the latter presented tumors.
source: Following heat-shock, patches of EGFP-labeled supernumerary NSCs were observed for all enhancer-FLP(D) lines, with both hs-mFLP5;FOFO2.0-CD2miRs-GAL4miRs (controls) and hs-mFLP5;FOFO2.0-prosmiRs-GAL4miRs but only the latter presented tumors (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5a.

claim: The heat-shock regime that led to best tumor reproducibility was a double pulse of 1.5 hr each, with the first at the end of embryogenesis and a second during L1.
source: Concerning reproducibility, in the first instance, we were looking for symmetry between brain lobes, suggestive of near-complete extent of recombination within the enhancer domain. The heat-shock regime that led to best tumor reproducibility in this regard was a double pulse of 1.5 hr each, with the first at the end of embryogenesis and a second during L1 (when brain NSCs are still quiescent), thus providing two doses of mFLP5 ~24 hr apart without intervening NSC divisions (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding demonstrated in Figure 6.

claim: With hs-mFLP5;FOFO2.0-bratmiRs-GAL4miRs following heat-shock, patches of EGFP-labeled supernumerary NSCs were efficiently generated with stg14-FLP(D) but rarely observed for R19H09-FLP(D).
source: With hs-mFLP5;FOFO2.0-bratmiRs-GAL4miRs following heat-shock, patches of EGFP-labeled supernumerary NSCs were efficiently generated with stg14-FLP(D) but rarely observed for R19H09-FLP(D) (Figure 6a), reflecting the different expression dynamics of the two enhancers.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6a.

claim: Tumors were largest when cells were delivered double-loads of each of the recombinases (2 hs in homozygous enhancer-FLP(D) animals) and smallest when a single dose of each recombinase was provided.
source: Tumors were largest when cells were delivered double-loads of each of the recombinases (2 hs in homozygous enhancer-FLP(D) animals) and smallest when a single dose of each recombinase was provided (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6b.

claim: The double-load of mFLP5 and of FLP(D) greatly reduced tumor asymmetry between lobes.
source: The double-load of mFLP5 and of FLP(D) greatly reduced tumor asymmetry between lobes (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 6c.

claim: The authors were able to generate spatiotemporally controlled lineage-restricted labeled CNS tumors in a single stock in the absence of the GAL4/UAS system.
source: In summary we were able to generate spatiotemporally controlled lineage-restricted labeled CNS tumors in a single stock in the absence of the GAL4/UAS system.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the achievements demonstrated throughout the Results section.

claim: The study validates the tool for independent genetic manipulations in strictly non-overlapping domains, which is transformative for the study of cell non-autonomous effects.
source: This validates our tool for independent genetic manipulations in strictly non-overlapping domains, which is transformative for the study of cell non-autonomous effects.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the experimental demonstrations.

claim: The design opens up for the first time the ability to perform efficient genome-wide screening for non-autonomous effects on deleterious genotypes.
source: Our design opens up for the first time the ability to perform efficient genome-wide screening for non-autonomous effects on deleterious genotypes.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application based on the demonstrated capabilities.

claim: Employment of 4 miRs is efficacious and permits simultaneous downregulation of multiple genes in the labeled domain.
source: We show that employment of 4 miRs is efficacious and permits simultaneous downregulation of multiple genes in the labeled domain
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful knockdown of both tumor suppressors and GAL4.

claim: T2A sequences can be added for simultaneous overexpression of coding sequences in addition to that for a reporter.
source: furthermore, T2A sequences can be added for simultaneous overexpression of coding sequences in addition to that for a reporter.
evidence: This is stated as a design feature based on known properties of T2A.

claim: The system can be used to refine spatial domains, intersecting various enhancer-recombinases (in addition or not to hs control).
source: The system can be used also to refine spatial domains, intersecting various enhancer-recombinases (in addition or not to hs control).
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application based on the modular design.

claim: The sensitivity of the FOFO design allowed definition of STOP cassettes appropriate to curb even short Pol II readthrough.
source: The sensitivity of our design (with miR expression inducing a readily detectable and quantifiable phenotype even in non-labeled cells) allowed us to define STOP cassettes appropriate to curb even short Pol II readthrough.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: The discrete number of progenitors from which tumors are initiated provided a convenient platform to quantify Flippase cross-reaction.
source: The discrete number of progenitors from which tumors are initiated provided a convenient platform to quantify Flippase cross-reaction and revealed low-level cross-reaction of FLP(D) with mFRT71 sites, not described before.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the experimental system.

claim: Low-level cross-reaction of FLP(D) with mFRT71 sites was not described before.
source: The discrete number of progenitors from which tumors are initiated provided a convenient platform to quantify Flippase cross-reaction and revealed low-level cross-reaction of FLP(D) with mFRT71 sites, not described before.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding from the study.

claim: The degree of tumor reproducibility reported differences in expression dynamics of the lineage-restricted enhancers.
source: The degree of tumor reproducibility reported differences in expression dynamics of the lineage-restricted enhancers (e.g. as seen by more asymmetric brat tumors with R19H09-FLP(D) than with stg14-FLP(D)) and incomplete extent of recombination within the enhancer domain.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: Reproducibility could be improved by increased loading of recombinases.
source: Reproducibility could be improved by increased loading of recombinases so in cases where reproducibility is desired we recommend using multiple copies of recombinase transgenes.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation based on the experimental findings.

claim: The presence of larval neural tumors induces developmental delay whose extent is proportional to tumor size.
source: For example, the presence of larval neural tumors induces developmental delay whose extent is proportional to tumor size (our unpublished observation)
evidence: This is stated as an unpublished observation by the authors.

claim: Neural tumors in some lineages lead to adult sub-lethality (presence of adults bearing tumors in a sub-Mendelian proportion).
source: and in some lineages leads to adult sub-lethality (i.e. presence of adults bearing tumors in a sub-Mendelian proportion).
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: The extent of developmental delay and of adult escapers can be used as first-pass proxies for tumor size for speedy screening of non cell-autonomous modifiers.
source: Therefore, the extent of developmental delay and of adult escapers can be used as first-pass proxies for tumor size, for speedy screening of non cell-autonomous modifiers of these parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective screening strategy based on the observations.

claim: A FOFO version containing a Luciferase reporter can be generated to use Luciferase activity as an efficient method of quantifying reporter-expressing cells in homogenized tissue.
source: Additionally, a FOFO version containing a Luciferase reporter can be generated in order to use Luciferase activity as an efficient method of quantifying reporter-expressing cells (in our case tumor volume) in homogenized tissue (Homem et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application with citation support.

claim: Custom-made FOFO tools can be applied to any desired topic and cell types.
source: Custom-made FOFO tools can be applied to any desired topic and cell types.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application based on the modular design.

claim: Control flies (those with miRs against CD2) will be available 'off the shelf'.
source: Control flies (those with miRs against CD2) will be available 'off the shelf' and experimental ones can be generated by either gene synthesis or modification of the control plasmid; or by CRISPR-modification of control host flies.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective resource availability.

claim: The FOFO tool allows sparse labeling of specifically targeted cells (sparseness achieved by short heat-shock and cell-type targeting provided by enhancer-FLP), which is extremely useful for studying cellular morphology and/or migration.
source: Furthermore, even without gene perturbations, the FOFO tool allows sparse labeling of specifically targeted cells (sparseness achieved by short heat-shock and cell-type targeting provided by enhancer-FLP), which is extremely useful for studying cellular morphology and/or migration.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application based on the demonstrated capabilities.

claim: The principles of the FOFO design can be applied to other model organisms where distinct site-specific recombinases work, such as zebrafish and mouse.
source: The principles of the FOFO design can be applied to other model organisms where distinct site-specific recombinases work, such as is the case for zebrafish and mouse (Nern et al., 2011; Olorunniji et al., 2016; Carney and Mosimann, 2018; Yoshimura et al., 2018) for refined spatial and/or temporal control of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application with citation support.

claim: In zebrafish, heat-shock induced gene expression allows for faster and/or focal induction of gene expression as compared to drug-induced expression.
source: In zebrafish, heat-shock induced gene expression allows for faster and/or focal induction of gene expression as compared to drug-induced expression (Halloran et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Direct translation of a FOFO tool for large-scale screening for non-autonomous effects is feasible in zebrafish by employment of the GAL4/UAS or Q/QUAS systems.
source: Direct translation of a FOFO tool with the aim here described (large-scale screening for non-autonomous effects) is feasible in zebrafish by employment of the GAL4/UAS or Q/QUAS systems (Subedi et al., 2014; Kawakami et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application with citation support.

claim: In mouse, focal thermal shock can be induced by Brownian motion of iron oxide nanoparticles when subject to a magnetic field.
source: In mouse, one-way thermal shock can be focally-induced (thus minimizing unwanted damage of most cells) is by Brownian motion of iron oxide nanoparticles when subject to a magnetic field.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Iron oxide nanoparticles injected into specific tissues remain static and can be visualized by magnetic resonance imaging.
source: Once injected into specific tissues, these nanoparticles remain static and can be visualized by magnetic resonance imaging (Pankhurst et al., 2003), which means the site of injection, and therefore of heat-shock, can be located any time post-injection.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Induction of tumorigenesis focally in specific cell types by a combination of heat-shock and a cell-type-specific recombinase, in a way that allows identification of exactly where the tumor was initiated, will be invaluable to study the earliest events in mammalian tumorigenesis.
source: Translating the example of this study into mice, induction of tumorigenesis focally in specific cell types by a combination of heat-shock and a cell-type-specific recombinase, in a way that allows identification of exactly where the tumor was initiated, will be invaluable to study the earliest events in mammalian tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a prospective application.

claim: The earliest events in mammalian tumorigenesis are largely a 'black box' in in vivo mammalian cancer studies, with assumed extrapolation from in vitro findings, since by the time a tumor can be visualized it is usually already of a substantially advanced stage.
source: This is largely a 'black box' in in vivo mammalian cancer studies, with assumed extrapolation from in vitro findings, since by the time a tumor can be visualized it is usually already of a substantially advanced stage.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in mammalian cancer research.

claim: In pros mutant lineages, GMCs revert to NSCs in type I, and to INPs in type II.
source: In pros mutant lineages, GMCs revert to NSCs in type I, and to INPs in type II
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Brat mutation affects only type II lineages, in which INPs revert to NSCs.
source: brat mutation affects only type II lineages, in which INPs revert to NSCs.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Each brain lobe consists of central brain and optic lobe regions.
source: each brain lobe consists of central brain and optic lobe regions
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Each central brain contains ~100 NSCs: eight type II and ~90 type I.
source: each central brain contains ~100 NSCs: eight type II (purple circles) and ~90 type I (red circles).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.
